nodes.title: Grade 11
nodes.description: CAPS Grade 11

nodes.title: Physical Sciences
nodes.description: Physical Sciences — Grade 11 — CAPS Curriculum

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: Term 1 — Mechanics and Electrostatics. Weeks 1–10. Formal assessment: Control test.

assessmentStandards: Control test

nodes.title: Vectors in Two Dimensions
nodes.description: Resultant of vectors using the component method on a Cartesian plane. Application of the Pythagoras theorem for magnitude and trigonometric ratios for direction. Tail-to-head and parallelogram methods. Resolving vectors into Rx and Ry components. Closed vector diagrams.

assessmentStandards: Determine the resultant of vectors using the component method on a Cartesian plane
Apply Pythagoras theorem to calculate the magnitude of a resultant vector
Use trigonometric ratios to determine the direction of the resultant
Apply tail-to-head and parallelogram methods
Resolve vectors into Rx and Ry components
Identify and draw closed vector diagrams

nodes.title: Newton's Laws
nodes.description: Normal force and frictional force. Static friction (fs_max = μsN) and kinetic friction (fk = μkN). Force diagrams and free-body diagrams. Resolving forces on inclined planes. Newton's first law (inertia, seatbelts). Newton's second law (Fnet = ma) for single objects on horizontal, inclined, and vertical surfaces, and two-body systems. Newton's third law (action-reaction pairs).

assessmentStandards: Define and distinguish normal force and frictional force
Apply fs_max = μsN for static friction and fk = μkN for kinetic friction
Draw force diagrams and free-body diagrams
Resolve forces on inclined planes
State Newton's first law and apply it to situations involving inertia (e.g. seatbelts)
Apply Newton's second law (Fnet = ma) to single objects on horizontal, inclined, and vertical surfaces
Apply Newton's second law to two-body systems
Identify Newton's third law action-reaction pairs

nodes.title: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
nodes.description: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂/d². Gravitational acceleration g = GM/r². Weight vs mass. Concept of weightlessness.

metadata.capsReference: Mechanics: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
assessmentStandards: State and apply Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂/d²
Derive and apply gravitational acceleration: g = GM/r²
Distinguish between weight and mass
Explain the concept of weightlessness

nodes.title: Electrostatics
nodes.description: Coulomb's law F = kQ₁Q₂/r² applied to 1D and 2D right-angle problems. Electric field as a region of force. Field patterns for point charges, two charges, and a charged sphere. Electric field E = F/Q and E = kQ/r². Problems involving up to three charges in a line.

assessmentStandards: State and apply Coulomb's law: F = kQ₁Q₂/r²
Solve 1D and 2D right-angle Coulomb's law problems
Define electric field as a region where a test charge experiences a force
Draw and interpret electric field patterns for point charges, two charges, and charged spheres
Apply E = F/Q and E = kQ/r²
Solve problems involving up to three charges in a line

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: Term 2 — Electromagnetism, Electric Circuits, Atomic Combinations, and Intermolecular Forces. Weeks 1–11. Formal assessment: Control test.

assessmentStandards: Control test

nodes.title: Electromagnetism
nodes.description: Magnetic field near a current-carrying wire. Right Hand Rule. Magnetic field patterns for a wire, loop, and solenoid. Magnetic flux (Φ = BAcosθ). Faraday's Law (emf = −NΔΦ/Δt). Direction of induced current.

assessmentStandards: Describe the magnetic field near a current-carrying wire
Apply the Right Hand Rule to determine field direction
Draw and interpret field patterns for a wire, loop, and solenoid
Define magnetic flux and apply Φ = BAcosθ
State and apply Faraday's Law: emf = −NΔΦ/Δt
Determine the direction of induced current

nodes.title: Electric Circuits
nodes.description: Ohm's law. Ohmic and non-ohmic conductors. Series and parallel circuits with up to four resistors. Power formulae (P = W/Δt, P = VI, P = I²R, P = V²/R). Internal resistance (emf = IR_ext + Ir). Kilowatt-hour and electricity cost calculations.

assessmentStandards: State and apply Ohm's law
Distinguish between ohmic and non-ohmic conductors
Analyse series and parallel circuits with up to four resistors
Apply power formulae: P = W/Δt, P = VI, P = I²R, P = V²/R
Apply the internal resistance equation: emf = IR_ext + Ir
Calculate electricity costs using kilowatt-hour

nodes.title: Atomic Combinations
nodes.description: Definition of a chemical bond. Lewis diagrams. Valence electrons. Covalent bonds (single, double, triple). Molecular shapes (linear, angular, pyramidal, tetrahedral). Bonding and lone pairs. Dative covalent bonds. Electronegativity. Polar and non-polar bonds. Bond energy and bond length.

assessmentStandards: Define a chemical bond
Draw Lewis diagrams for molecules
Identify valence electrons
Describe and distinguish single, double, and triple covalent bonds
Predict and explain molecular shapes: linear, angular, pyramidal, tetrahedral
Distinguish bonding pairs from lone pairs
Explain dative covalent bonds
Define electronegativity and use it to classify bonds as polar or non-polar
Relate bond energy and bond length

nodes.title: Intermolecular Forces
nodes.description: Distinction between intermolecular and interatomic forces. Van der Waals forces (London dispersion, dipole-dipole, dipole-induced dipole). Hydrogen bonding. Ion-dipole forces. Relationship between intermolecular forces and molecular mass. Effect on boiling point, melting point, vapour pressure, and solubility.

assessmentStandards: Distinguish intermolecular forces from interatomic (intramolecular) forces
Describe London dispersion, dipole-dipole, and dipole-induced dipole forces
Explain hydrogen bonding and its origin
Describe ion-dipole forces
Relate the strength of intermolecular forces to molecular mass
Explain the effect of intermolecular forces on boiling point, melting point, vapour pressure, and solubility

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: Term 3 — Quantitative Aspects of Chemical Change, Energy and Change, Acids and Bases, and Ideal Gases. Weeks 1–11. Formal assessment: Control test.

assessmentStandards: Control test

nodes.title: Quantitative Aspects of Chemical Change
nodes.description: The mole concept, Avogadro's number, and molar mass. Avogadro's law and molar gas volume. Mole calculations: n = m/M, n = V/Vm, n = particles/NA. Concentration c = n/V. Percentage composition. Empirical and molecular formulae. Stoichiometric calculations including limiting reagents. Percentage yield.

assessmentStandards: Define the mole, Avogadro's number, and molar mass
State and apply Avogadro's law and molar gas volume
Apply n = m/M, n = V/Vm, and n = particles/NA
Calculate concentration using c = n/V
Determine percentage composition of compounds
Determine empirical and molecular formulae
Perform stoichiometric calculations including identification of limiting reagents
Calculate percentage yield

nodes.title: Energy and Change
nodes.description: Heat of reaction (ΔH). Exothermic and endothermic reactions. Activation energy and activated complex. Potential energy versus course of reaction graphs.

assessmentStandards: Define heat of reaction (ΔH)
Distinguish between exothermic and endothermic reactions
Define activation energy and activated complex
Draw and interpret potential energy vs course of reaction graphs

nodes.title: Acids and Bases
nodes.description: Names and formulae of common acids and bases. Arrhenius and Brønsted-Lowry theories of acids and bases. Conjugate acid-base pairs. Amphiprotic substances. Acid-base indicators. Volumetric analysis and neutralisation reactions.

metadata.capsReference: Types of Reactions: Acids and Bases
assessmentStandards: Write names and formulae of common acids and bases
Describe the Arrhenius theory of acids and bases
Describe the Brønsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases
Identify conjugate acid-base pairs
Define and identify amphiprotic substances
Describe the function of acid-base indicators
Perform volumetric analysis calculations for neutralisation reactions

nodes.title: Ideal Gases
nodes.description: Molecular motion, collisions, and average speeds. Ideal gas vs real gas. Boyle's law (V inversely proportional to P at constant T). Temperature as a measure of average kinetic energy. Pressure arising from molecular collisions.

assessmentStandards: Describe molecular motion, collisions, and average speeds in a gas
Compare ideal and real gases
State and apply Boyle's law: V ∝ 1/P at constant temperature
Explain temperature as a measure of average kinetic energy of particles
Explain gas pressure in terms of molecular collisions

nodes.title: Term 4
nodes.description: Term 4 — Types of Reactions (continued), Revision, and Final Examination. Weeks 1–10. Formal assessment: Final examination (Paper 1 Physics 150 marks, Paper 2 Chemistry 150 marks).

assessmentStandards: Final examination Paper 1: Physics (Vectors, Newton's laws, Electrostatics, Electromagnetism, Electric circuits) — 150 marks
Final examination Paper 2: Chemistry (Atomic combinations, Intermolecular forces, Ideal gases, Quantitative aspects, Energy and change, Types of reaction) — 150 marks

nodes.title: Types of Reactions (continued)
nodes.description: Acid-base reactions: neutralisation and salt preparation. Redox reactions: oxidation numbers, electron transfer, oxidising and reducing agents. pH scale and pH calculations. Balancing redox reactions using the half-reaction method.

metadata.capsReference: Types of Reactions: Redox and pH
assessmentStandards: Describe and perform acid-base reactions including neutralisation and salt preparation
Assign oxidation numbers in compounds and ions
Identify electron transfer, oxidising agents, and reducing agents in redox reactions
Explain and apply the pH scale
Perform pH calculations
Balance redox reactions using the half-reaction method

nodes.title: Revision and Final Examination
nodes.description: Revision of all Term 1–4 content (weeks 4–7). Final examination weeks 8–10: Paper 1 Physics 150 marks (Vectors in 2D, Newton's laws, Electrostatics, Electromagnetism, Electric circuits). Paper 2 Chemistry 150 marks (Atomic combinations, Intermolecular forces, Ideal gases, Quantitative aspects of chemical change, Energy and change, Types of reactions).

assessmentStandards: Revise all physics and chemistry content from Terms 1–4
Final examination Paper 1 Physics — 150 marks: Vectors in Two Dimensions, Newton's Laws, Electrostatics, Electromagnetism, Electric Circuits
Final examination Paper 2 Chemistry — 150 marks: Atomic Combinations, Intermolecular Forces, Ideal Gases, Quantitative Aspects of Chemical Change, Energy and Change, Types of Reactions
